title: Customizable player views
summary: Connect independently replaceable input, camera, HUD and appearance adapters for each local player.

blocks.text: A player view ties a seat, viewport, player and controlled target to independently owned adapters. Games supply compatible input/entity routing, camera, HUD instruments and appearance. No adapter is mandatory: headless controls and non-flight viewers can use only the parts they need. This service never creates a world, changes physics, polls devices or advances time.

Each adapter exposes its underlying resource identity plus rebind, release and dispose. Mutable resources cannot be shared between players or roles. Controllers recheck entity ownership through their existing control-target adapter; seat/view identity never grants authority. Every old input/gesture is released before a new target is published. A failed rebind removes the adapters and leaves the view neutral until configured again. Failed configuration retains old adapters with intent released.

Standard controller, camera and HUD wrappers borrow their underlying instances unless ownership is explicitly owned. The view always owns its wrapper and disposes it when replaced or removed. Keep a camera borrowed when LocalViews already owns it. Camera wrappers enforce matching viewport identity. To wrap the same underlying resource differently, remove its old wrapper first. Separate players need independent instances.

Appearance adapters and custom parts own their typed settings, validation and rendering hooks. A future editor can configure those providers or replace one player’s parts without putting game-specific theme, vehicle or physics schemas into this foundation. The flight host currently adopts the HUD/appearance lifecycle; its legacy flight input/camera wiring is still explicit. The Survey example composes controller and local camera through the same player-view service.
